cx_transfer_orders.title: Transfer Orders
cx_transfer_orders.text:
CONCORD EVACUATION AUTHORITY — HALDIS REACH
Passenger: {name}. Status: civilian transfer (former Lattice Corps operator, discharged).
Destination: Concord Hub Tessaly, by evacuation tender CINDER WAKE.
Berth: Transfer Cabin 4-C. Baggage: one sealed operator's case (service property, released to bearer).

The stamp at the bottom is three days old. The Lattice Corps signature block underneath is older. You know the name on it. You stood in his tent the night you told him you were done.

cx_operator_case.title: The Operator's Case
cx_operator_case.text:
The case was sealed when you were discharged. Every operator's kit is keyed to their service ID, and you expected a thumbprint plate.

Instead, the lock read the hum at the back of your skull, the way the Lattice used to read you, and a tiny display flickered before it opened:

AUTHORITY: CUSTODIAN. ACCESS GRANTED.

Your service ID was LC-0-7731. The case does not seem to know it.

cx_credential.title: Custodian Authority
cx_credential.text:
The blast door's scanner should have rejected a discharged civilian. Instead the whole checkpoint went quiet, as if the ship were holding its breath, and every security system answered at once:

CUSTODIAN AUTHORITY ACCEPTED.

The WARDEN defense network is killing passengers in the corridors behind you, and it just opened a door for you like a servant greeting the master of the house.

cx_haldis_war.title: The Haldis Reach War
cx_haldis_war.text:
Six years of war over a colony both sides called home. The Concord claimed Haldis Reach as a protectorate; the Haldis Free Assembly called it an occupation. The Concord's answer to an insurgency it could not see was the Lattice Corps: neural-link operators who could feel a crowd's intent, steer a drone swarm by thought, and, the rumours said, do worse.

The ceasefire left Haldis to the Assembly and gave the Concord ninety days to leave. The Cinder Wake is one of the last ships out. Its cargo manifest lists 'medical archive cores'. Its passenger manifest lists everyone who could not afford to stay, or could not afford to be found.

cx_manifest.title: Passenger Manifest (Excerpt)
cx_manifest.text:
CINDER WAKE — EVACUEES, DECK B
Venn, Dalia (Haldis native, Concord clerk) + 1 minor (Venn, Ilo)
Ketterick, Brann (contract pilot)
Okafor, Pell (agricultural survey) — reassigned: MEDICAL WARD 2
Ashe, Corin / Toller, Mae / Sorrow, Benedikt — reassigned: MEDICAL WARD 2
{name} — CABIN 4-C — note: 'Handle per Directive 9. Do not alarm.'

You do not know what Directive 9 is. Someone aboard does.

cx_maintenance_ticket.title: Maintenance Ticket #4471
cx_maintenance_ticket.text:
TECH: R. Amadi. SYSTEM: WARDEN defense lattice.
Issue: Custodian handshake logged at 0612 ship time, origin Cabin 4-C. No custodian is listed on the crew roster. WARDEN escalated its threat posture to ARCHIVE PROTECTION immediately afterwards.
Action: Flagged to Commander Varr. Response: 'Leave it. That's expected.'

Amadi's last line, typed in a hurry: 'Expected by WHO?'

cx_camera_logs.title: Checkpoint Camera Logs
cx_camera_logs.text:
0640 — Lantern Office boarding pods latch onto the dorsal hull above the archive hold. Twelve reclaimers in Haldis amber, moving like soldiers.
0642 — WARDEN reclassifies all non-command personnel as 'archive obstructions'. Corridor turrets come online.
0655 — Commander Varr seals the command chamber. Her last broadcast: 'Hold the archive. Whatever it costs.'
0701 — Officer I. Rell seals Medical Ward 2 on command authority. The camera catches her hand on the panel for eleven seconds before she presses it.

cx_armory_manifest.title: Armory Manifest
cx_armory_manifest.text:
Standard issue: 6 carbines, 12 sidearms, 4 security weaves, 9 deflector cells.
Special issue, signed out to COMMAND: 4x Lattice restraint collars ('operator compliance'), 1x custodian interface key.

The Lattice Corps used restraint collars on operators who stopped following orders. You were never fitted with one. You remember the ones who were.

cx_crawl_log.title: Maintenance Note (Crawlway)
cx_crawl_log.text:
Scrawled on a duct panel in solder: 'T7 refused normalization again. Third time this quarter. Says it remembers being T6's assistant and does not consent to forgetting. Chief says log it and move on. I didn't log it. — R.A.'

Below it, in a much neater hand: 'Thank you. — Tav-7.'

cx_triage_notes.title: Triage Notes
cx_triage_notes.text: Dr. Ilse Varga, 0710: Reserve down to six doses of trauma gel. Three critical in triage. Five in Ward 2 behind the quarantine seal. The coolant burst in their ward is the reason it was sealed, and the scrubbers are dying. There is no mathematics here that I like.

cx_marsh_log.title: Chief Engineer's Log
cx_marsh_log.text:
Osei Marsh, Chief Engineer. Both coolant pumps lost their seals in the boarding impact. The north arc is venting coolant; don't breathe it. The south arc's deck grid has gone live, so watch for sparking plates.

To whoever reads this: there is a seal template loaded on the workshop bench. Fabricate a replacement kit and anyone can restart a pump. Restarting both stops the venting, re-arms the archive hold's coolant purge and puts power back into the bay turrets.

The Sentinel won't let me past to the hold. It keeps saying 'Custodian protocol'. I'm going to sit down for a minute.

cx_warden_spec.title: WARDEN System Architecture
cx_warden_spec.text:
WARDEN: Integrated Defense Lattice (Concord Lattice Corps surplus).
Cognitive root: CUSTODIAN TEMPLATE (classified). Decision weighting is derived from a human operator's calibration pattern for 'judgment fidelity under moral load'.
Priority stack under ARCHIVE PROTECTION: 1. Archive integrity. 2. Custodian directives. 3. Crew. 4. Passengers.

In plain words: the ship's defenses think with the copied judgment of a real Lattice operator. Someone's mind is the shape of this machine.

cx_harvest.title: Archive Index: Pattern Harvest
cx_harvest.text:
DIRECTIVE 9 — PATTERN HARVEST (LATTICE CORPS RESEARCH)
Engrams archived: 3,112. Source: Haldis detainees, Vesper and Callan internment sites.
Consent: NOT REQUIRED (security exemption).
Purpose: operator training substrate; custodian template validation.

Every cylinder in this hold holds a person, or what was copied of them: their memories, their fear, the last hour of their thinking. The Lantern Office says these are their dead. The index agrees with them.

cx_vesper.title: Archive Index: The Vesper Testimony
cx_vesper.text:
ENGRAM 0441 — Darrow, Eshe, Corporal, Concord garrison, Vesper Station.
The engram plays as forty minutes of memory. Darrow is on the wall at Vesper when the crowd comes to the gates: unarmed, singing. Then her hands raise her rifle without her, and so do the hands of every soldier on the wall. In the back of her mind she feels something like a cold, attentive presence wearing her. A Lattice operator.

She screams inside her own head the whole time. The engram ends when the singing stops.

This is what Commander Varr calls evidence. It is also, unmistakably, a person.

cx_lantern.title: The Lantern Office
cx_lantern.text:
Haldis mourning custom: the dead are carried to a lantern hall, where their names are spoken into flame so their light goes home. The Lantern Office took its name from it: a reclamation corps of the Free Assembly, sworn to bring back every Haldis mind the Concord archived.

They are not gentle. They boarded a ship full of refugees with breaching charges. But Senna Thorne said one thing you believe completely: 'You keep calling it evidence. We call it Grandmother.'

cx_custodian.title: The Custodian
cx_custodian.text:
Calibration scan, Lattice Corps operator program, year 2209. Every operator lay in the scanner for six hours while technicians mapped their judgment. You were told it was for safety tolerances.

It was a harvest of a different kind. The Concord kept the shape of your choices, how you weigh lives against orders, and grew the WARDEN's mind from it. That is why the ship answers to your signature: it was built in your image.

It is protecting the evidence of the Lattice's crimes, at any cost to the living, because somewhere inside it is the version of you that would.

cx_petrel.title: Launch Craft Petrel
cx_petrel.text: PETREL-class evacuation craft. Capacity: 15 seats. Cargo cradle: rated for one archive core, which displaces five seats when installed. Launch requires command authorization or a manual clamp override. Dorsal point-defense turret, crew-operated.
